title: Add a Date Stamp to a Photo Already Taken on iPhone
description: iPhone can't print the date on a photo. Here's how to add the orange, old-camera date stamp using the day the photo was taken, plus corner, color and size tips.
h1: How to add a date stamp to a photo on iPhone, even one already taken
card_summary: The glowing orange date of 90s film cameras, taken from the day the photo was shot.
quick_answer: The iPhone Camera and Photos apps store the date in the photo's info but cannot print it on the picture. In Halatto, open the photo, tap Date stamp and pick a corner: the orange date is read from the day the photo was taken, in the '26 11 19 style of film cameras. Adjust Direction, Color and Size, then save.
intro: The orange date in the corner is the most recognizable detail of a 90s film photo. Point-and-shoot cameras exposed it onto the film with tiny LEDs, so it glows slightly and sits on top of the picture.
Here is how to get that exact look on an iPhone photo, using its real capture date.

sections.heading: Can the iPhone add a date stamp on its own?
paragraphs: No. Swipe up on a photo in Photos (or tap the i button) and you will see the date and time, which you can also adjust. That information lives in the file's metadata; it is not drawn on the image, and it disappears in many apps and screenshots.
To make the date part of the picture you need an app that draws it on. Utility apps put a plain timestamp on photos for documentation. Halatto draws the retro orange one, matched to film looks.

sections.heading: What a real film date stamp looks like
list: Format: 'YY MM DD with an apostrophe, for example '26 11 19.
Color: glowing orange-red, a little soft at the edges.
Position: usually the bottom right corner, sometimes rotated on vertical shots.

steps.heading: Step by step: date stamp in Halatto

items.name: Open the photo
items.text: Pick the photo in Halatto. Optionally choose a film look first so the date sits on film color.

items.name: Open Date stamp
items.text: Tap Date stamp and choose one of the four corners. The off icon removes it.

items.name: Set direction
items.text: Use Direction for a horizontal date, or a vertical one going up or down along the edge.

items.name: Adjust color and size
items.text: Drag Color to move from classic orange toward yellow or green, and Size to make it smaller or bigger.

items.name: Save
items.text: Tap the checkmark and save or share the photo.

tips.heading: Tips
items: Keep the date small; on old prints it was a few millimetres high.
Bottom right on a dark area of the photo glows best.
Pair it with Snap 400 or Titan 38 for a 90s point-and-shoot look.
Stamp every photo of a trip the same way so the set reads like one roll of prints.

faq.question: Can I add a date stamp to a photo already taken?
faq.answer: Yes. Open any photo from your library in Halatto and tap Date stamp. The date comes from the day the photo was taken, so a picture from last summer gets last summer's date, not today's.

faq.question: Which date does Halatto use?
faq.answer: The day the photo was taken, read from the photo's information.

faq.question: Can I add a date stamp to a screenshot or saved image?
faq.answer: Yes. Any image in your library works; the date comes from the information saved with it.

faq.question: Can I remove the date stamp later?
faq.answer: Yes. Reopen the edit in Halatto, open Date stamp and turn it off.
